facts.t: Report published 13 May 2026.
Coverage snapshot is January 2026.
The release is an interim update to Connected Nations 2025.
Connected Nations 2025 used July 2025 data.
Decent broadband is at least 10 Mbit/s down and 1 Mbit/s up.
Lower-priced satellite plans changed affordable-decent-broadband eligibility.
Mobile coverage is based on predictions from four mobile network operators.
5G standalone coverage is reported as rollout continues.
Gigabit-capable availability reached 89%.
Gigabit-capable availability covered 27.1 million homes.
July 2025 gigabit-capable availability was 87%.
July 2025 gigabit-capable availability covered 26.4 million homes.
The gigabit availability increase was 2 percentage points.
The reported homes increase was approximately 0.7 million.
Affordable decent broadband residual was about 4,000 premises.
Fixed-line or FWA decent-broadband residual was 39,000 premises.
The fixed-line/FWA residual fell by 5,000 from July 2025.
Fixed and mobile data downloads are published separately.
Vodafone and Three predictions remain reported separately until integration.
About 7,000 commercial premises were excluded from the USO estimate.
Dataset provides BDUK's current view of OMR determinations.
Dataset distinguishes current gigabit connection and future plans.
Dataset includes BDUK delivery plans for commercially unviable premises.
Premises base uses the latest AddressBase Premium epoch available at OMR time.
Non-postal and demolished premises are filtered from the premises base.
An absent UPRN may be demolished, derelict, or a new build outside the epoch.
The release is split into 318 local-authority CSV files.
UPRN is numeric and may contain up to 12 digits.
struprn preserves UPRN integrity in software imports.
bduk_recognised_premises indicates whether a connection would provide benefit.
White status means no qualifying gigabit network and none likely within three years.
Grey/Black status can include current or planned qualifying infrastructure.
Under Review includes unverified current claims or delivery-risk evidence.
Contract scope distinguishes Initial, Deferred, and In Procurement.
Final coverage date is the initial-scope final payment date, not a parcel guarantee.
June 2026 release uses the January 2026 OMR.
BDUK applies automated and manual assurance checks.
The release is not designed as a backwards-looking delivery record.
About 3.7% of intervention premises are in more than one intervention.
Around 4,900 GIS premises are absent because OS now categorises them as demolished.
QMI documents quality characteristics and production methods.
QMI is intended to reduce the risk of data misuse.
The responsible organisation is DSIT's BDUK Directorate.
Statistics measure premises receiving gigabit coverage because of BDUK subsidy.
Administrative geography sources include ONS, NISRA and Scottish Government.
AddressBase Premium is a source dataset.
Ofcom premises- and postcode-level data are used for Ofcom-base estimates.
UPRN is the statistical unit and does not change over time.
BDUK's premises base differs from Ofcom's premises base.
The time series covers 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2026.
